record.paper_title: Open questions in massive star research
record.original_question: When a core-hydrogen-burning star in a close binary accretes enough mass to grow substantially, to what extent is it rejuvenated, meaning how far does its convective core grow and how much fresh hydrogen is mixed into that core across the stabilizing mean-molecular-weight gradient? The unresolved issue is whether semiconvective mixing is efficient enough for nearly complete rejuvenation, and whether observed contact binaries and their period-change measurements support or rule out that scenario.

evidence.quote: To what extent mass gainers are rejuvenated is one of them most important and most longstanding unsolved questions in binary evolution.

The problem is that any mixing of hydrogen into the core has to overcome the strongly stabilising mean molecular weight gradient. This process is likely controlled by semiconvection (Braun & Langer 1995), a thermal timescale mixing process of uncertain efficiency (e.g., Schootemeijer et al 2019).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a core-hydrogen-burning star of mass $M_1$ in a close binary that, through Roche-lobe overflow from its companion, accretes a substantial amount of mass $\Delta M$ on a thermal timescale, so that its new total mass $M_1+\Delta M$ is significantly larger than $M_1$. Before accretion, the star possesses a convective core of mass $M_{\rm c}$ surrounded by a radiative envelope across which a stabilizing mean-molecular-weight gradient $\nabla_\mu = d\ln\mu/d\ln P > 0$ has built up due to prior hydrogen burning. After accretion, the equilibrium convective core of a single star of mass $M_1+\Delta M$ would be of mass $M_{\rm c}^{\rm new} > M_{\rm c}$, but the actual growth of the convective core into the chemically inhomogeneous region is impeded by $\nabla_\mu$ and is governed by semiconvective mixing, a doubly-diffusive process whose efficiency parameter $\alpha_{\rm sc}$ (in, e.g., the Langer prescription) is poorly constrained.

Define the rejuvenation fraction
$$f_{\rm rej} \;=\; \frac{M_{\rm c}^{\rm act}-M_{\rm c}}{M_{\rm c}^{\rm new}-M_{\rm c}}\in[0,1],$$
where $M_{\rm c}^{\rm act}$ is the actual post-accretion convective-core mass and $\Delta X_{\rm c}$ the corresponding amount of fresh hydrogen mixed into the convective core across the $\mu$-barrier.

Determine:

(a) the functional dependence of $f_{\rm rej}$ and $\Delta X_{\rm c}$ on the semiconvective efficiency $\alpha_{\rm sc}$, the pre-accretion central hydrogen abundance $X_{\rm c}$, the mass ratio $\Delta M/M_1$, and the strength of the $\mu$-barrier;

(b) whether semiconvective mixing can be efficient enough to produce nearly complete rejuvenation ($f_{\rm rej}\to 1$); and

(c) whether the observed population of massive contact binaries, together with their measured orbital period derivatives $\dot P/P$ (which depend on the internal structure evolution of the accretor through mass transfer and tidal coupling), are consistent with nearly complete rejuvenation or instead require $f_{\rm rej}$ to be bounded away from $1$.
artifact.category_tag: stellar evolution and binary star modeling
artifact.status_search_result: The question remains open. Recent 2025 work introduces phenomenological prescriptions (e.g., limiting convective-core overshoot based on the molecular-weight gradient) that reduce the rejuvenation efficiency of accretors and improve agreement with the observed mass-ratio distribution of massive contact binaries, suggesting that nearly complete rejuvenation is disfavored. However, the underlying efficiency of semiconvective mixing and a definitive observational determination of the rejuvenation fraction have not been established.

status_evidence.title: Effects of limited core rejuvenation on the properties of massive contact binaries
status_evidence.snippet: By limiting core rejuvenation through convective-core overshoot tied to the molecular gradient, the predicted mass-ratio distribution shifts away from unity, improving agreement with observed massive contact binaries.
status_evidence.claim: Recent modeling indicates that limiting rejuvenation efficiency is required to match observations, implying nearly complete rejuvenation is not supported.

status_evidence.title: Reverse mass transfer and rejuvenation in a massive contact system
status_evidence.snippet: The rejuvenation of accretors and the efficiency of semiconvection remain uncertain and actively investigated in massive close binaries.
status_evidence.claim: The rejuvenation question is still being actively studied in 2025.

status_evidence.title: Detailed models of interacting short-period massive binary stars
status_evidence.snippet: Whether stars rejuvenate depends on the still poorly understood efficiency of semiconvection.
status_evidence.claim: Semiconvective efficiency, and hence rejuvenation, remains poorly constrained.
